title: Best Hour to Close the Shop
statement:
A shop kept a visitor log for one day: a string log where log[h] is 'Y' if at least one customer came during hour h, and 'N' if nobody did.

The owner wants to pick a closing hour j between 0 and n (inclusive, where n = log.length). The shop is open for hours 0 … j − 1 and closed from hour j on. Closing at n means it never closes that day.

The penalty of a choice is:

  • +1 for every open hour with 'N' (staff waited for nobody), and
  • +1 for every closed hour with 'Y' (a customer found the door locked).

Return the closing hour with the smallest penalty. If several hours tie, return the earliest one.

examples.why: Never closing costs 1 (the single N). Closing at 1 costs 2: the two late customers are turned away. Nothing beats 1.
Closing at once costs 1 (the one Y). Every later hour adds at least as many empty open hours as it saves.
Hours 1 and 3 both cost 1. The earliest of the tied hours wins.

hints: Closing one hour later changes the penalty only because of that one hour. By how much?
Moving the closing time from j to j + 1 makes hour j open instead of closed: a 'Y' there lowers the penalty by 1, an 'N' raises it by 1.

Start a running score at 0 for j = 0 and walk the log, adding −1 for 'Y' and +1 for 'N'. The hour where the score is strictly lowest for the first time is the answer; the absolute penalty never needs to be computed.

explain.intuition:
You do not need the actual penalty, only how it changes. Sliding the closing hour from j to j + 1 flips exactly one hour, hour j, from closed to open. If a customer came then, you stop turning them away: −1. If nobody came, you now wait for nobody: +1.

So walk the string once with a running score that starts at 0 for j = 0. The score at each j equals the real penalty minus a constant (the number of Y's), so the smallest score marks the best hour. Update the best only on a strictly smaller score, and ties keep the earliest hour.
steps: For each hour h: add −1 if log[h] is 'Y', else +1. The score now belongs to closing hour h + 1.
If score < best, set best = score and bestHour = h + 1.
pitfalls: Only trying closing hours 0 … n − 1. Never closing (j = n) is allowed and is the answer for "YYYY".
Using <= when updating the best, which returns the latest tied hour instead of the earliest.
Counting the hour j itself as open. At closing hour j the shop is already closed during hour j.

solutions.title: Recount for every closing hour
solutions.idea: For each j, count N's before j and Y's from j on. Keep the first j with the smallest total.

solutions.title: Prefix counts
solutions.idea: Count all Y's once. Then walk j from 0 to n keeping N's seen so far and Y's still ahead, so each penalty is O(1).

solutions.title: Running score of changes
solutions.idea: Only the change matters: each Y lowers the penalty of closing later by 1, each N raises it by 1. Track the first minimum of that running score.

followups: Each wasted open hour costs 2 and each turned-away customer costs 3. What changes?
The log streams in hour by hour. Can you report the best closing hour so far after each new hour?
